FIBA Under-17 World Championship|2016 Spain]] | [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Markus Anthony Howard''' (born March 3, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Saski Baskonia]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]], where he was a two-time [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and led the nation in scoring in the 2019–20 season. ==High school career== Howard began his high school career at [[Perry High School (Gilbert, Arizona)|Perry High School]] in [[Gilbert, Arizona]]. As a freshman, he started in the backcourt with his brother and averaged 23 points per game, leading his team to the state semifinals.{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Heller|url=http://www.eastvalleytribune.com/varsityxtra/tribune-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year-markus-howard/article_1b7a1c72-c748-11e3-9087-001a4bcf887a.html|title=2013–2014 Tribune Boys Basketball Player of the Year: Markus Howard|work=[[East Valley Tribune]]|date=April 20, 2014|access-date=December 29, 2018}} He committed to [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] following his freshman season.{{cite web|first=Richard|last=Obert|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/recruiting/2014/08/27/gilbert-perrys-markus-howard-commits-to-asu-basketball/14718849/|title=Markus Howard from Gilbert Perry commits to ASU basketball|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=August 27, 2014|access-date=December 29, 2018}} After a sophomore season where he averaged 32.4 points per game, Howard decommitted from Arizona State and reopened up his recruitment.{{cite web|first=Richard|last=Obert|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/recruiting/2015/03/16/perry-guard-markus-howard-decommits-from-asu/24858029/|title=Perry guard Markus Howard decommits from ASU|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=March 16, 2015|access-date=December 29, 2018}} For his junior season, Howard transferred to national basketball power [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]].{{cite web|first=Ashton|last=Ferguson|url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/arizona-transfer-howard-excited-about-playing-for-findlay-prep/|title=Arizona transfer Howard excited about playing for Findlay Prep|work=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]]|date=June 19, 2015|access-date=December 29, 2018}} During his junior season at Findlay Prep, where he led the team in scoring, Howard announced that he would [[reclassification (education)|reclassify]] to the class of 2016 and signed with [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].{{cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/findlay-preps-markus-howard-reclassifies-to-2016-commits-to-marquette|title=Findlay Prep's Markus Howard reclassifies to 2016, commits to Marquette|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 3, 2016|access-date=December 29, 2018}} ==College career== As a freshman at Marquette University, Howard entered the starting lineup and averaged 13.2 points per game and led the country in [[Three-point field goal|three-point]] shooting at 54.7%. He was named to the 2017 [[Big East Conference]] All-Freshman team.{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Steele|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2018/10/25/stronger-markus-howard-ready-carry-big-load-marquette/1757988002/|title=Marquette guard Markus Howard has added muscle to help grow his game|work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]]|date=October 25, 2018|access-date=December 29, 2018}}{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Velazquez|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2017/03/05/marquettes-markus-howard-named-big-east-all-freshman-team/98770032/|title=Marquette's Markus Howard named to Big East all-freshman team|work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]]|date=March 5, 2017|access-date=December 29, 2018}} As a sophomore, Howard became one of college basketball's top scorers. On the season, Howard averaged 20.4 points per game and was named second-team All-Big East.{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Steele|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/2018/03/04/marquettes-markus-howard-named-all-big-east-second-team/393498002/|title=Marquette's Markus Howard named to all-Big East second team|work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]]|date=March 4, 2018|access-date=December 29, 2018}} He also finished the season with the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]]'s second-best [[free throw percentage]] (93.8%). Going into his junior season of [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19]], Howard earned national preseason recognition, appearing on the watch lists for the [[Wooden Award]], the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]] and the [[Bob Cousy Award]] for top [[point guard]]. Howard was also selected preseason first-team All-Big East.{{cite web|url=https://gomarquette.com/news/2018/10/25/mens-basketball-howard-and-hauser-earn-big-east-honors-as-mu-is-picked-second.aspx?path=mbball|title=Howard and Hauser earn BIG EAST honors as MU is picked second|work=[[Marquette Golden Eagles]]|date=October 25, 2018|access-date=December 29, 2018}} In Marquette's non-conference schedule, Howard recorded two 45-point games, against ranked teams [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] and [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo]]. In the Buffalo win, Howard scored 40 of his total in the second half.{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Caron|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/12/21/markus-howard-45-points-marquette-win-buffalo-highlights|title=Markus Howard Explodes for 40-Point Second Half as Marquette Knocks Off Buffalo|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=December 21, 2018|access-date=December 29, 2018}} He scored a career-high 53 points in an overtime win over [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]] on January 9, 2019, breaking a Big East single-game record.{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Boone|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/marquettes-markus-howard-explodes-for-52-points-in-overtime-win-vs-providence/|title=Marquette's Markus Howard explodes for 52 points in overtime win vs. Providence|work=[[CBSSports.com]]|date=January 4, 2018|access-date=December 29, 2018}} Howard became Marquette's all-time leading scorer when he contributed 38 points in an 88–53 victory against [[Loyola Greyhounds men's basketball|Loyola (Md.)]] in the team's season opener of his senior year. He was named Big East player of the week on November 11, 2019.{{cite news |title=Marquette's Howard, Villanova's Robinson-Earl Nab First #BIGEASThoops Weekly Honors |url=https://www.bigeast.com/news/2019/11/11/mens-basketball-marquettes-howard-villanovas-robinson-earl-nab-first-bigeasthoops-weekly-honors.aspx |access-date=November 12, 2019 |work=Big East Conference |date=November 11, 2019}} On November 29, Howard scored 51 points in a 101–79 win over [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]. He became the third player to score 50 points in a game in three straight seasons, joining [[Wayman Tisdale]] and [[Pete Maravich]]. In addition, since he scored 40 points in the previous match, he joined Maravich, [[Johnny Neumann]], and [[Bob Pettit]] as the only players in major conferences to score 40 points on back-to-back days.{{cite news |title=Marquette's Markus Howard drops 51, joins elite company |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28190815/marquette-markus-howard-drops-51-joins-elite-company |access-date=December 1, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 29, 2019}} Howard sat out a game against [[Jacksonville Dolphins men's basketball|Jacksonville]] on December 4 with a concussion.{{cite news |last1=Steele |first1=Ben |title=Marquette 75, Jacksonville 56: Golden Eagles win without Markus Howard |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2019/12/04/marquette-beats-jacksonville-markus-howard-sits-out-concussion-protocol/2607310001/ |access-date=December 9, 2019 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]] |date=December 4, 2019}} On February 12, 2020, Howard scored 24 points and had five rebounds and two assists in a 72–71 loss to [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]]. He became the Big East's all-time leading scorer in league games, surpassing [[Lawrence Moten]]'s 1,405 points.{{cite news |title=Marquette's Markus Howard now Big East's career points leader |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28690662/marquette-markus-howard-now-big-east-career-points-leader |access-date=February 13, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 12, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Howard was unanimously selected to the First Team All-Big East.{{cite news |last1=Steele |first1=Ben |title=Marquette's Markus Howard is named to all-Big East first team |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/2020/03/08/marquette-senior-guard-markus-howard-named-all-big-east-first-team/4995834002/ |access-date=March 8, 2020 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]] |date=March 8, 2020}} Howard averaged 27.8 points and 3.3 assists per game as a senior.{{cite news |last1=Dauster |first1=Rob |title=NBC Sports College Basketball All-American Teams |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/03/10/college-basketball-all-american-teams/ |access-date=March 16, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 10, 2020}} During his time at Marquette University, Howard accumulated 2761 points. ==Professional career== ===Denver Nuggets (2020–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Howard signed a [[two-way contract|two-way deal]] with the [[Denver Nuggets]]{{cite news |last1=Steele |first1=Ben |title=Marquette's Markus Howard gets a chance with the Denver Nuggets after going undrafted |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2020/11/18/marquettes-markus-howard-not-picked-nba-draft/6338010002/ |access-date=November 19, 2020 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]] |date=November 18, 2020}} whose official announcement was released on November 30, 2020.{{cite web|title=Nuggets sign guard Markus Howard to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-markus-howard-202011|date=November 30, 2020|website=nba.com|access-date=November 30, 2020}} On May 13, 2021, Howard scored a career-high 15 points in a 114–103 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web|date=2021-05-13|title=Nuggets' Markus Howard sets new career-high in win over Timberwolves|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2021/05/13/nuggets-markus-howard-new-career-high-timberwolves/|access-date=2021-05-13|website=The Rookie Wire}}{{Cite Timberwolves|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2021/05/13/nikola-jokic-leads-nuggets-past-timberwolves/|access-date=2021-05-13|website=The Denver Post|quote=Both Markus Howard (15 points) and Vlatko Cancar (14) enjoyed career-highs and helped offset Karl-Anthony Towns' 20-point, 11-rebound effort for Minnesota.}} He re-signed with the Nuggets on a new two-way contract on August 15, 2021.{{Cite web |title=Nuggets Re-Sign Markus Howard To Two-Way Deal |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/08/nuggets-re-sign-markus-howard.html |access-date=2022-10-19 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en-US}} Howard appeared in 31 games and had two 20-point performances during the 2021–22 season.{{Cite web |title=Nuggets 2021–22 Player Reviews: Markus Howard |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-2021-22-player-reviews-markus-howard |access-date=2022-10-19 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} ===Cazoo Baskonia (2022–present)=== On July 17, 2022, the Spanish club [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] announced the signing of Howard into a two-year deal.{{cite web|url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/355737-markus-howard-nuevo-director-de-juego-de-cazoo-baskonia.html|title=Markus Howard, nuevo director de juego de Cazoo Baskonia|publisher=acb.com|date=July Partizan|Partizan]] on October 14, 2022, and 30 points against [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] on October 19, 2022.{{Cite web |title=Markus Howard explodes for 33 points as Baskonia defeats Partizan in OT |url=https://basketnews.com/news-179334-markus-howard-explodes-for-33-points-as-baskonia-defeats-partizan-in-ot.html |access-date=2022-10-19 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2022-10-19 |title=Baskonia prevails at home over feisty Crvena Zvezda |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1406904/baskonia-crvena-zvezda-euroleague/ |access-date=2022-10-19 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}} On October 4, 2023, Howard signed a new contract with Baskonia through 2026 and on May 14, 2024, he agreed upon a further extension through 2028. ==National team career== Howard has represented the United States in [[FIBA]] play on two occasions. In 2015, he was a member of the gold medal-winning US team in the [[2015 FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]]. Howard then won a gold medal at the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] in Zaragoza, Spain.{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Stevens|url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/06/markus-howard-usab-veteran.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160614211242/http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/06/markus-howard-usab-veteran.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 14, 2016|title=USA Basketball Training Camp Veteran: Markus Howard|work=[[USA Basketball]]|date=June 12, 2016|access-date=December 29, 2018}} In the U17 tournament, Howard averaged 11.9 points and 2.6 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.anonymouseagle.com/2016/7/3/12091556/marquette-basketball-markus-howard-wins-fiba-u17-gold-medal-team-usa|title=Incoming Marquette Basketball Freshman The brothers were teammates for one season at Perry High.{{cite web|first=Richard|last=Obert|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/01/11/college-basketballs-splash-brothers-got-their-start-perry-former-perry-hoops-coach-could-tell-early/1025757001/|title=College basketball's 'Splash Brothers' Jordan and Markus Howard got their start at Perry High|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=January 11, 2018|access-date=December 29, 2018}} He is of Puerto Rican descent.[https://www.elvocero.com/deportes/fbpur-pone-el-ojo-en-markus-howard/article_0b28bad8-d561-11e7-bfc8-574b962314ba.html Fbpur pone el ojo en Markus Howard (Spanish)] Howard is very public about his Christian faith. Howard explained the reason why he wears number 0 by saying, "First and foremost, I'm a Christian before anything else. I'm a son [of God], so I want to be sure that my number meant something and it represented something.
